definition: Circumspect means cautious and careful about consequences.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word circumspect. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know circumspect should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Before signing anything, Grandmother was circumspect about the lottery win: she asked the lawyer to walk her through everything that claiming it would set in motion.

Careful is milder than circumspect — checking the mirror, reading the label, it looks only at the task in front of it; circumspect looks all the way around the task, asking what each move would set off.
Distrustful goes further than circumspect — the circumspect witness weighs each answer before giving it; the distrustful one assumes the question is a trap.

Guarded describes the fence you keep around your own words and plans — answers kept short, intentions unshown. Circumspect is wider than a fence: it looks all the way around an action before taking it, weighing consequences. A guarded person reveals little; a circumspect one may speak freely, after checking the ground.

Wary is alertness to a danger you already suspect — the hiker eyeing the sky, the buyer who has been burned before. Circumspect needs no threat in view: it walks a decision's whole perimeter before stepping, danger or none. Wary watches the other party; circumspect watches your own next move.

Offered twice his salary to join the startup, Dario spent a circumspect month before answering: he read the funding documents, called two engineers who had quit, and asked what would happen to his visa if the company folded.
He said yes in the end — but on terms that survived the layoffs when they came.
Circumspect is the precise word because it means cautious and careful about consequences — from the Latin for 'looking around': he walked the whole decision's perimeter before stepping.
Hesitant would say he merely paused; circumspect says the pause was spent looking.
Circumspect describes caution exercised in advance — what you say to reporters, sign with landlords, post online.
Its unit-mate prudence is the parent virtue, good judgment overall; circumspect is that judgment at the moment of speaking or acting.
Wary leans toward suspicion of others; circumspect watches your own next step.

Lindqvist's team caught the strange radio signal, her postdocs wanted a press conference within the week.
Lindqvist was circumspect.
Before saying a word in public, she walked the announcement's whole perimeter: What if the signal was a satellite?
What would a false alarm cost the observatory's next grant?
Who else needed to verify the data first?
She was not hiding the result -- every line of data went onto a public server that same month.
